newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hogs seen steady-up $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hogs seen steady-up $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest cash hog prices Tuesday were seen mostly steady, with a chance of being up $0.50 per cwt in parts of the eastern Corn Belt if harsh weather hits the area, dealers and packer buyers said.

Portions of southern Illinois and central Indiana could get freezing rain overnight, which may limit hog marketings, sources there said. A central Indiana buyer said rain this afternoon was turning to ice on trees and power lines.
Top prices for Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs delivered to the plant Tuesday were seen steady at $56.50 to $57.00.

Top prices at plants in Illinois were seen steady to up $0.50, ranging from $55.50 to $56.00. Indiana/Ohio hog prices were seen steady, at a top of $55.00 to $55.25, but could turn higher if icy road conditions curtail hog movement, the dealers said.

However, lower pork prices could limit cash hog price strength, sources said. Fresh pork prices at midday were quoted down $1.00 to $4.00 per cwt for hams and steady to $2.00 lower for pork bellies, USDA said. There were 23.0 loads of pork cuts sold.
